messages.subject: Shuffle Problem
parts:
Hello All,

I've got a problem I've been struggling with for days. Here's the
deal.

I've got some bug report data:
identifier name ver class wmc dit noc cbo rfc lcom
1 ant 1.7 org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.rmic.RmicAdapterFactory 3 1 0
10 18 3
2 ant 1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.perforce.FStatP4OutputHandler 5
2 0
3 ant 1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.junit.OutErrSummaryJUnitResultFormatter
1
4 ant 1.7
org.apache.tools.ant.taskdefs.optional.perforce.P4HandlerAdapter 8 1 9
13 20

I truncated it so it would fit in this window. Essentially, it's 5
merged datasets from the PROMISE software engineering repository (Ant,
Lucene, Camel, etc). I want to calculate the total number of bugs for
the Ant classes, lucene classes, camel classes, etc. I iterate this
with the Map Reduce below. I'm expecting Hadoop/Rhipe to 'shuffle/
merge' the keys, but it's not doing it.

library(Rhipe)
rhinit(TRUE,TRUE,buglevel=2000)

map.test <- expression({
y <- do.call("rbind",map.values)

if(nrow(y) > 0)
{
for( i in 1:nrow(y))
{
x<-y[i, ]
key<-x[2] #codebase
value<-as.numeric(x[25]) #bugs
rhcollect(key,value)
}
}

})

reduce <- expression(
post={
rhcollect(reduce.key, reduce.values)
}
)

mapred <-
list(rhipe_map_buff_size=20,mapred.task.timeout=0,mapred.reduce.tasks=1)
z <-
rhmr(map=map.test,reduce=reduce,inout=c("sequence","sequence"),ifolder="/
apacheOut/blocks_01/p*"
,ofolder="/apacheOut/blocks_04",mapred=mapred,
combiner=FALSE)
rhex(z)


The Map function kicks out 3113 records, as I would expect, each with
the name of the software and the number of bugs like this:
(lucene, [0,1,4,0,0...])

However, when I look at the results from the debugging reduce I'm
using, it's the same list that comes out of the Map ... all 3113
records, without them being shuffle/merged. Tried dozens of things...
nothing seems to matter. Not sure if it makes a difference, but I'm
using Cloudera's CDH 3.5 running in Pseudo Distributed mode in a
single VM.

Would appreciate any ideas as to why the shuffle/merge isn't occuring.

Thanks,
Jeremy

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Shuffle Problem
parts:
Hello,
1) What is an element of map.values? A line look likes

?
I shall assume that y is a matrix of fields corresponding to the
example you gave.
2nd field is codebase, 25th field is the number of bugs.
I guess you want total number of bugs by codebase?
Better map:
map.test <- expression({  y <- do.call('rbind',map.values)  ## how can
nrow(y) == 0???  if(nrow(y)>0){    apply(y[,c(2,25)],1,function(r){
  rhcollect( r[1], as.numeric(r[2]))    })  }})
So you want to aggregate your values e.g.

 (lucene, [0,1,4,0,0...])
(I thought sum?)
1) If you wanted an aggregate
reduce <- expression(  pre={ y <-  c() }  ,reduce = { y <- c(y,
unlist(reduce.values)) }  ,post = { rhcollect(reduce.key, y ) })
mapred <- list(rhipe_map_buff_size=20,mapred.task.timeout=0)z <-
rhmr(map=map.test          ,reduce=reduce
,inout=c("seq","seq"),ifolder="/apacheOut/blocks_01/p*"
,ofolder="/apacheOut/blocks_04"          ,mapred=mapred,
,combiner=TRUE)rhex(z)

2) You want a sum?reduce <- expression(  pre={ y <-  0 }  ,reduce = {
y <-  y+ sum( unlist(reduce.values),na.rm=TRUE) }  ,post = {
rhcollect(reduce.key, y ) })
The other code is the same.
Hope this helpsSaptarshi

parts:
Thanks Saptarshi! I learn by example, so it definitely helps. And, I
tested your recommendations and they worked perfectly!

If you have a moment, would mind explaining to me why your example
worked and my attempt failed? When I study the output from my Map
function and compare to your Map output, they appear to be the same.
However, when I run my output through the reducer example you
provided, it still comes out as a list of 3113 records. So the
"special sauce" is in the Mapper, or so it would seem. Is there some
added dimensionality to the data that prevents this from being
shuffled? I was using Shekar's example (http://groups.google.com/
group/brumail/browse_thread/thread/244a9af9633772a8) as the basis ...
it seems to work for him, but not when I used it... just trying to
understand why.

for( i in 1:nrow(y))
{
x<-y[i, ]
key<-x[2] #codebase
value<-as.numeric(x[25]) #bugs
rhcollect(key,value)
}
Because the example you provided (below) was shuffled

Separate from that question, I am under the impression that if the
data can be shuffled/merged, it always is. In other words, if I send
a list of key/values, where the key is text, and the value is a
number, shouldn't the shuffle always merge the set on the key -e.g.
(lucene, [0,1,4,0,0...])?


Thanks!
jeremy
